questions.key_step: Power-reduce $\cos^4x$ with $\cos2x$ and integrate.
questions.justification: One familiar move (power reduction) with routine arithmetic; options allow a check.

questions.key_step: Differentiate the integral equation to a linear ODE and solve with $1/x^2$.
questions.justification: Leibniz rule then standard linear ODE; chained routine steps, no insight.

questions.key_step: Differentiate with upper limit $t^2$ and substitute $t=\pi/2$.
questions.justification: A single Leibniz-rule step; the only care is the chain-rule factor $2t$.

questions.key_step: Substitute $e^x=t$, integrate $\ln(t+\sqrt{1+t^2})$ by parts, and match a messy option.
questions.justification: Substitution plus by-parts plus careful logarithm simplification; routine but error-prone.

questions.key_step: Evaluate $\min\{x^2,x-[x]\}$ on $[0,1)$ and $[x-\ln x]$ on $[1,2]$.
questions.justification: Reading two piecewise definitions correctly, then two easy integrals.

questions.key_step: Split $[e^{1-x}]$ at $1-\ln2$ and $1$.
questions.justification: Monotone floor splitting with an answer to be read as $\alpha-\ln2$; short chain.

questions.key_step: $\int_0^1f(\lambda x)d\lambda=\frac1x\int_0^xf$ turns the equation into a separable ODE.
questions.justification: Hidden substitution then ODE with a parameter $a$ solved from $f(16)$; numerical answer, several stages.

questions.key_step: Recognise $1^\infty$ form and evaluate $\lim\frac{I(t)-1}t$.
questions.justification: Integral, $1^\infty$ limit with logarithm of a mixed expression, then matching constants; no options.

questions.key_step: Split at $\frac\pi{48}$ and $\frac\pi6$ and add the sine pieces.
questions.justification: Two breakpoints from modulus and floor; routine integrals, cos terms cancel.

questions.key_step: Skew-line distance gives $k=\frac32$; split $[x^2]$ at $1,\sqrt2$.
questions.justification: Two independent routine parts stitched by $k$; calculations are short.

questions.key_step: Convert to $t=\tan x$ and split $\frac{t^2}{(1+t^2)(1+t+t^2)}$ into partial fractions.
questions.justification: Non-obvious $\tan$ conversion with $\sin x\cos x$ in the denominator, then partial fractions and a completed square.

questions.key_step: King property then $\int_0^\pi\frac{dx}{1-\cos^2t\sin^2x}=\frac{\pi}{\sin t}$.
questions.justification: King property on $x\,F(\sin x)$, a standard tan-integral with a parameter, then a simple final integral.

questions.key_step: By parts to get $r_k=\frac{7k+8}{7k+7}$, so the sum is $\sum(k+1)$.
questions.justification: Recurrence by parts with a hidden pattern; once seen the sum is trivial.

questions.key_step: Count the breakpoints $\sqrt n$ and $\sqrt{2n}$ and collect surd coefficients.
questions.justification: Many pieces for two floor functions; one slip changes $a$, $b$ or $c$ and there are no options.

questions.key_step: Read the sum as $\int_0^1\frac{1-x^2}{(1+x^2)\sqrt{1+x^4}}dx$ and substitute $t=x+\frac1x$.
questions.justification: Riemann-sum recognition plus a non-routine $x+\frac1x$ substitution, then another substitution; numerical answer.

questions.key_step: $f$ is odd, so it drops; pair $x$ with $-x$ to remove $\frac1{1+e^x}$.
questions.justification: Two standard properties chained, then one by-parts integral.

questions.key_step: Slope relation makes the denominator vanish at $x=3$; apply L'Hopital.
questions.justification: Short chain; the only step is spotting the $\frac00$ form.

questions.key_step: $1-\sin2x=(\sin x-\cos x)^2$ and split at $\frac\pi4$.
questions.justification: One identity, one split and routine evaluation of surds.

questions.key_step: Solve $\frac{10x}{x+1}=1,4,9$ for breakpoints.
questions.justification: Floor of a monotone function with three simple breakpoints.

questions.key_step: $f(x)+f(1-x)=1$ makes $x\to1-x$ legitimate and gives $M=N-M$.
questions.justification: Property of $f$ must be found, then King property on an unusual interval; no options.
